title: External-user and Experience Cloud access fundamentals
objectives: Distinguish authenticated Experience Cloud members from unauthenticated guest users who share one guest user record per site.
Explain that guest users get record access through guest user sharing rules, not manual sharing, under Secure guest user record access.
Keep external organization-wide defaults and guest profiles as least-privilege baselines, not clones of internal System Administrator.
Refuse to treat Experience Cloud as 'just another profile' without checking licenses, sharing, and guest policies.
diagnostic_question: A public Experience Cloud site shows LAB_FAQ articles to people who never log in, while LAB_Customer should see only their own Cases after login. A teammate wants to manually share a Case to the guest user. What is the guest identity, what sharing mechanism is allowed, and what would you not clone from internal Salesforce?
definition: Experience Cloud sites connect customers and partners. Unauthenticated visitors use a site guest user: Salesforce creates a guest profile and one guest user record per site, and all guest visitors share that identity. Secure guest user record access is enabled and cannot be disabled; guests get Read Only record access only through guest user sharing rules, a special criteria-based sharing rule, not manual sharing. Guest users are not automatically the owner of records they create; a default active user becomes owner. Authenticated external users use external licenses, profiles, and sharing that are not the same as internal users. ([Securely Share Sites with Guest Users](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_secure_community.htm); [Review Guest User Access](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.shr_guest_user_access.htm))
why_it_matters: Guest access is unauthenticated. A casual manual share or a cloned internal profile can publish CRM data to the internet. Interviewers listen for guest sharing rules, the one-guest-user-per-site model, default owners, and the refusal to use internal sharing habits on a public site.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel. The lobby brochure rack is the guest user: everyone who walks in without a key shares the same public identity. They only get what the hotel explicitly put on the rack (guest user sharing rules), not a front-desk one-off key (manual sharing). A registered guest with a room key is an authenticated Experience Cloud member with an external license. Staff badges are internal users. Do not give the brochure rack a staff master key.
deeper_explanation: When you create an Experience Cloud site, Salesforce creates a guest user profile and a site guest user record. All unauthenticated visitors share that one guest user record per site and therefore the same access. ([Guest user setup](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_secure_community.htm))

Secure guest user record access is enabled in orgs with Experience Cloud sites and cannot be disabled. Guests can be granted Read Only access to records only through guest user sharing rules. Guest users cannot access records via manual sharing. ([Guest policies](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_secure_community.htm); [Review Guest User Access](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.shr_guest_user_access.htm))

Records created by guest users are assigned to a default active user in the org, not kept as guest-owned. Configure that default owner deliberately. ([Guest user setup](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_secure_community.htm))

Use the guest user profile to control public object, field, and app access. Test as the guest before go-live. The Guest User Sharing Rule Access Report in Setup helps see what guests can reach. Do not invent license names or edition matrices; inspect the org's Experience Cloud licenses.

Authenticated external users still have object, field, and record gates (SEC-003/004), plus external OWD. Sharing sets and super-user access are neighboring Experience Cloud tools; treat their exact behavior as Needs verification in current Help rather than reciting unofficial matrices.

mental_model.analogy: A hotel: lobby brochure rack = guest user (shared public identity), rack policy = guest sharing rules, room key = authenticated external member, staff badge = internal user.
useful_mapping: brochure rack → one guest user record per site
what is on the rack → guest user sharing rules (Read Only)
front-desk one-off key → manual sharing (not allowed for guests)
room key guest → authenticated Experience Cloud user
who files a lobby form → default owner, not the guest user
where_it_breaks: External licenses and sharing sets are more specific than 'room keys'.
API and site preference controls add extra guest gates not visible in a hotel lobby.
Partner versus customer sites differ by license; do not invent which objects each license includes.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Unauthenticated visitors share one guest user per site. They get records only via guest user sharing rules, not manual sharing. Authenticated external users have licenses and external sharing. Do not clone internal admin profiles for either.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I split public versus logged-in. Public: guest profile least privilege, criteria-based guest sharing rules, test with the Guest User Sharing Rule Access Report, default owner for creates. Logged-in customers: external license, then the same object/field/record gates. I mention Secure guest user record access cannot be turned off. I do not invent license object lists.

terminology.plain: A Salesforce-branded site for customers or partners.
terminology.precise: An Experience Cloud (community/site) with its own membership, guest identity, and sharing. Creating it creates guest profile and guest user artifacts.
terminology.example: LAB_Support_Site for synthetic FAQ and Case defection tests.
terminology.non_example: The internal Lightning app for employees.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Salesforce Sites / Site.com remnants: still in the guest-security policy family; confirm product name in org.

terminology.plain: The shared identity of people who use the site without logging in.
terminology.precise: One guest user record per site, tied to the guest profile. All anonymous visitors share that access level.
terminology.example: Two browsers on LAB_Support_Site without login share the same guest identity.
terminology.boundary: Not a second internal Salesforce license seat in the usual employee sense.

terminology.plain: The allowed way to grant guests Read Only record access.
terminology.precise: A special criteria-based sharing rule for unauthenticated guest users. Manual sharing to guests is not allowed under Secure guest user record access.
terminology.example: Share LAB_FAQ__c records where LAB_Public__c is true to the site guest.
terminology.non_example: Clicking Share on a Case and picking the guest user.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Ordinary sharing rules for internal groups (SEC-004).
terminology.boundary: Warning: this grants access without login credentials.

terminology.plain: A logged-in customer or partner on the site.
terminology.precise: An authenticated user with an Experience Cloud / community license, not the guest user. Object and record access still apply.
terminology.example: LAB_Customer logs in and sees their own Cases.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Internal user with a Salesforce license.
terminology.boundary: Exact license names Need verification in the org.

terminology.plain: The internal user who owns records guests create.
terminology.precise: Guests are no longer automatically owners of records they create; assign a default active user.
terminology.example: LAB_Web_Owner owns web-to-case-like records created from the public form.
terminology.non_example: Leaving ownership on the guest user as a security strategy.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Queue assignment: a possible neighboring routing design; verify in org.

terminology.plain: The record-access baseline for external users.
terminology.precise: Review Guest User Access describes setting a restrictive baseline for external users so data is not shared by default unless authorized.
terminology.example: External OWD Private for Case in a lab site.
terminology.non_example: Copying internal Public Read/Write to external because 'it is the same object'.
terminology.boundary: Confirm Sharing Settings UI for external access in the org.

options.D: Guests do not have a user record

interview_questions.question: How does Experience Cloud guest access work?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unauthenticated visitors share one guest user per site. The guest profile sets CRUD/FLS. Records are granted only through guest user sharing rules, Read Only. Manual sharing is not allowed. Test incognito.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start with identity. Creating a site creates the guest profile and guest user. Secure guest user record access cannot be disabled. I keep the guest profile empty of CRM objects unless a public row type exists. I use criteria-based guest sharing rules and the access report. Creates go to a default owner. Authenticated customers are a different user. I do not clone System Administrator.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Support_Site public FAQs via guest rule; Cases never on the guest.
tradeoffs: Public SEO content vs CRM exposure
follow_ups: Can you turn the secure setting off?

interview_questions.question: Guest versus authenticated external user versus internal user?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Internal: employee Salesforce license. External member: logged-in customer/partner license. Guest: shared unauthenticated site identity. Three sharing models; do not mix them.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw three columns. Internal uses SEC-002–004. Members use external OWD and Experience Cloud licenses I will verify in the org rather than reciting SKUs. Guests use guest profile plus guest sharing rules. MFA and login hours apply to people who log in, not to the guest. Interviewers ding people who say 'community user' as if it were one thing.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Admin, LAB_Customer, and incognito guest on LAB_Support_Site.
tradeoffs: One site with mixed audiences vs separate sites
follow_ups: What is a sharing set? (Needs verification)

interview_questions.question: Public FAQ plus private customer Cases on one site. Design the access?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Guest: FAQ object Read and a guest sharing rule on public FAQs only. No Case on the guest. LAB_Customer: authenticated external access to their Cases. Test both identities.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Situation: mixed public/private. Task: no Case leakage. Action: guest profile without Case Read, guest rule on LAB_Public FAQ rows, external OWD Private for Case, member sharing for own Cases. Incognito test plus customer test. Result: brochure rack has FAQs; room keys have Cases. I refuse a guest rule on Case 'for convenience.'
interview_questions.example: LAB_FAQ public flag true versus LAB_Customer Case.
tradeoffs: One object with a public flag vs a dedicated public object
follow_ups: How do you prove no Case in guest report?

interview_questions.question: A web form creates records as the guest. What do you configure besides the form?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Default owner for guest-created records, that owner's internal sharing, guest profile create permission only on that object if required, and no extra guest Read on unrelated CRM objects.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help moved ownership off the guest. If the default owner is a poorly shared user, internal teams will not see the work. If the owner is too privileged, you concentrate risk. I pick LAB_Web_Owner with a narrow role/share path. I test a synthetic submit incognito. I still do not manual-share to guest. API Enabled stays off unless a documented public API exists.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Web_Owner owns LAB_Web_Case; support group gets it via an internal sharing rule.
tradeoffs: Dedicated owner user vs a queue (verify)
Guest Create vs fully authenticated intake

interview_questions.question: The public site shows too many Accounts. How do you investigate?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Guest profile Account permissions, guest sharing rules, Guest User Sharing Rule Access Report, and an incognito test. I assume credential-less grants until proven otherwise.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Situation: data leak. Task: find the guest grant. Action: I do not log in as admin to 'see what guests see.' I read the access report, inspect criteria (maybe LAB_Public__c is null-true), and check object Read. I remove or tighten the guest rule under change control. Result: incognito no longer lists internal Accounts. I tell leadership guest rules are public by nature.
interview_questions.example: A guest rule with empty or overly broad criteria on Account.
tradeoffs: Taking the site private vs tightening criteria
weak_answer_warnings: Adding a manual share to 'fix' it

interview_questions.question: Where do sharing sets fit, and what do you not invent?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Sharing sets are a neighboring Experience Cloud mechanism for authenticated external users. I will not recite unofficial object matrices. I will say guests still cannot use them as a substitute for guest sharing rules.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Honesty is the interview. I know guest versus member. I know internal versus external OWD. Sharing sets, super users, and license SKUs change and are edition-sensitive, so I mark Needs verification and open current Help. I will still refuse System Administrator clones and guest Case Read. That combination beats a fake license table.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Customer login path: 'I would confirm sharing sets in Help if the requirement is access via Account relationship.'
follow_ups: What Help article would you open?

interview_questions.question: Public FAQ is blank for anonymous users but visible to you. First checks?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You are probably not the guest. Check guest object Read, FLS, guest sharing rule match, and whether public access is enabled. Test incognito.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce logged out. If I see the FAQ while logged in as admin, that proves nothing. I check the guest profile, the rule criteria against LAB_Public__c, and site public access. I check the Lightning page is exposed to guests. I do not grant the guest extra objects to 'make it show.' Result: incognito shows only matching FAQs.
interview_questions.example: Admin session versus Chrome incognito on LAB_Support_Site.
tradeoffs: More guest permissions vs fixing the rule
follow_ups: Experience Builder guest preview vs real guest?

interview_questions.question: Teach guest access with the hotel analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Brochure rack is the shared guest identity; rack policy is guest sharing rules; room keys are logged-in members; staff are internal. It breaks on license SKUs, sharing sets, and guest API site preferences.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk someone into the lobby without a key. I show they cannot get a front-desk one-off Case key. I check them in as LAB_Customer. I then break the hotel: Salesforce creates metadata (guest profile) not a paper rack; default owners file lobby forms; Review Guest User Access has API and visibility toggles. Close: credential-less grants are a go-live event.
interview_questions.example: Incognito FAQ versus LAB_Customer Case on the same hostname.
tradeoffs: Simple story vs Experience Cloud complexity
follow_ups: Where does SEC-004 external OWD apply?
